title: Ithaca #1899: native March 4 Flock termination directive
summary: Recovers the City of Ithaca Common Council agenda packet's native Flock termination resolution language and separates the legal directive from still-unproven technical offboarding execution.

methods: primary City of Ithaca agenda-packet review

data.question: What did Ithaca Common Council's native March 4, 2026 packet actually direct for Flock termination and equipment shutdown/removal?
data.method: Searched the current corpus first, reused the existing Ithaca offboarding identities, then reconciled the official Common Council agenda packet with contemporaneous reporting that the measure passed unanimously.
data.framework: Council directive, contract termination, platform disablement, credential revocation, sharing removal, physical removal, data deletion, audit preservation, and billing closeout are separate predicates.
data.scope: City of Ithaca municipal Flock termination/offboarding only; Cornell's separate campus deployment remains a distinct operator/network.
findings: The City of Ithaca's March 4 agenda packet directs the Acting City Manager to work with the City Attorney's Office to take all legally available steps to terminate the Flock contract at the earliest possible opportunity.
The resolution directs immediate suspension of Flock Safety services and equipment unless Common Council later reinstates or revokes that suspension.
The resolution states that upon contract termination Flock equipment is to be turned off and disconnected within fourteen days of enactment and related technology removed as soon as practicable.
Contemporaneous WSKG reporting says Common Council adopted the resolution unanimously on March 4, 2026.

These directives establish the public legal/implementation order but do not prove that Flock executed backend shutdown, credential revocation, sharing removal, deletion, or serial-level hardware removal on those dates.
conclusions: The previously unresolved native March 4 termination directive is now recovered at the City agenda-packet level.
Technical and data offboarding remain unresolved until native platform, credential, sharing, deletion, equipment, and closeout records are recovered.
recommendations: Recover Flock confirmation and platform/event logs establishing the exact shutdown timestamp.
Recover users/admins, credential revocations, Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks history, deletion/retention evidence, and partner notifications.
Recover serial-level reader removal work orders, custody/disposition records, and final billing/contract closeout.
Resolve any Ithaca Police ↔ Cornell Police directed access only from native sharing/audit evidence.
counterarguments: A council resolution can prescribe a deadline without proving vendor execution.
Physical removal may lag platform disablement, while physical absence does not itself prove credential revocation or data deletion.
limitations: This pass did not recover the executed vendor closeout package or native Flock exports.
The agenda packet is the legislative source; WSKG is used only to corroborate adoption and the unanimous vote.
unresolved: When did Flock actually disable the Ithaca tenant and reader services?
When were all user/admin/API credentials and directed sharing edges revoked?
What data was deleted, preserved, exported, or held, and under what authority?
When was each of the 22 municipal readers removed and what was its final custody/disposition?
Did any directed IPD↔CUPD access relationship exist?

classification_rules: Reuse the four canonical Ithaca offboarding targets already on main.

Platform disablement, credential revocation, sharing removal, hardware removal, data deletion, audit preservation, and contract/billing closeout remain separate evidence states.

findings.finding: The official March 4 City packet supplies the native termination/suspension/disconnect/removal directive missing from the prior #1899 pass.
WSKG independently reports unanimous adoption the same day.
No backend execution, credential/share revocation, deletion, or complete reader-disposition proof was recovered, so #1899 remains open.
